title: The DICTO Hexa: a cube of 8 DICTO Hexa Jewels, the Hexa-Key, and their 5 : 3 checkerboard filling of space
description: The DICTO Jewel is the regular dodecahedron of the Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli cell carved by the stella octangulas of its six neighbouring cells (volume 12 at cube edge 2); with stella octangulas it fills space. Eight DICTO Hexa Jewels (exact DICTO Jewels on a 2 × 2 × 2 block of cells, unsheared and passing through each other inside) form one solid, the DICTO Hexa : a cube of edge 4 with 24 outward roofs on its faces, volume 80 (6⅔ Jewels). No shear makes eight Jewels meet face to face as a cube; the Hexa exists only as overlapping exact Jewels. Hexas mate only window to window; at the FCC pattern of spacing 4 each has 12 neighbours, and the space between them is one solid, the DICTO Hexa-Key (8 stella octangulas and 12 double roofs, volume 48). Hexas and Hexa-Keys fill space as a checkerboard, 5 : 3 by volume , the Stella–Jewel Lattice one level up. The Hexa splits exactly into 8 cubes and 24 roofs, or into 4 whole and 4 trimmed Jewels. Clusters of eight Hexas, a diamond network of Hexas and stellas, and the absence of any turning join are also given. Not found in a web search (2026-10-09) or in our reference library (2026-10-15). title: The Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli Cell: all five Platonic solids on 13 points in one periodic cell, and a corner-sharing network of Kepler stars and icosahedra
description: Place Euclid's six roofs on a cube of edge 2 to obtain the regular dodecahedron, then reflect the twelve roof vertices back through the cube faces: they land exactly on a regular icosahedron inside the cube. Repeating the cube by translations of 2 gives a periodic structure, which we call the Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli (EKP) cell , with 13 nodes per cell, edge lengths in the chain 2 : 2/φ : 2/φ² (cube : dodecahedron : icosahedron), and space group Pm-3 (No. 200), nodes on Wyckoff positions 1b and 12j (0, y, z) with y = 1/(2φ), z = 1/(2φ²). Each roof vertex is a vertex of a neighbouring cell's icosahedron, and the ridges of the six neighbouring cells meet inside every cube as Pacioli's three interlocking golden rectangles. The cell nests all five Platonic solids (icosahedron ⊂ octahedron ⊂ stella octangula ⊂ cube ⊂ dodecahedron) with Kepler's great stellated dodecahedron around the icosahedron. From the same node set, great stellated dodecahedra on the even cells and icosahedra on the odd cells share only corners: the EKP network . All statements are checked by 48 exact or sampled tests. The individual nestings are classical; the periodic cell as a whole and the EKP network were not found in a literature search (2026-10-06, extended 2026-10-15) and we present them as candidates, not as priority claims. title: The DICTO Dodeca-13: the 13-dodecahedron cluster made solid, its gaps as two exact pieces, and separable finned units
description: A regular dodecahedron with a regular dodecahedron on each of its 12 faces is unique (each outer one is the centre's mirror image across the shared face) and is the first shell of the 120-cell laid flat. The 12 outer dodecahedra never overlap; they touch only along the centre's 30 edges, where three dodecahedra leave the well-known gap of 360° − 3 × 116.565° = 10.3048°. We show that the gaps are filled exactly by two kinds of congruent piece: 30 wedges (volume φ³/20 at edge 1), one on each edge of the centre, and 20 needles (volume (45 − 19√5)/600), one at each corner. Together the 63 pieces form one closed solid with no inner gap, the DICTO Dodeca-13 (volume 106.058472), whose outside is 72 regular pentagons, 60 thin trapezoids and 20 small triangles. Because each wedge is mirror-symmetric and each needle three-fold, the filled solid splits into a bare centre and 12 identical finned units that lift straight out. The cluster's convex hull, its densest translation packing (body-centred cubic, density 0.7154) and its relation to the DICTO-Star are also given. The 10.3° gap is known; the gap as two exact solid pieces, and the separable units, were not found in a literature search (2026-10-09). title: The DICTO-Star: an icosidodecahedron, 12 regular dodecahedra and 20 tridiminished icosahedra closing exactly in ordinary space
description: On each of the 12 pentagons of an icosidodecahedron place a regular dodecahedron, and on each of its 20 triangles a tridiminished icosahedron (Johnson solid J63), attached by its one triangle that borders only pentagons. The 33 regular-faced pieces (edge 1) meet only in whole faces and do not overlap. At every one of the icosidodecahedron's 60 edges the three dihedral angles add to exactly 360° (142.6226° + 116.5651° + 100.8123°), and the dodecahedron's face there is exactly a pentagon of the J63, so every edge and every corner is closed without a gap or filler. The volume is exactly (195 + 89√5)/3 ≈ 131.3367. With whole icosahedra in place of the J63s (a known virtual model) the pieces overlap; J63 is the icosahedron with exactly the three overlapping pyramids removed, which is what lets the arrangement exist exactly in flat space. The star does not continue into a space-filling by regular pieces. It was not found in a literature search (2026-10-09), and we present it as a candidate, not as a priority claim. title: The Chain of Karma: the icosahedron and the dodecahedron as endless shells of each other
description: We show that the regular icosahedron and the regular dodecahedron can each be filled exactly as a shell around the other, and that the two shells alternate without end. A dodecahedron of edge 1 is an icosahedron of edge 1/φ inside a shell of 12 pentagonal pyramids, 30 AXE and 20 CLEO; an icosahedron of edge φ² (the Lotus seed) is that dodecahedron inside a shell of 12 J11 (each an icosahedron with one pyramid cap removed), 30 AXE and 20 FUJI. Thus the nesting I(1/φ) ⊂ D(1) ⊂ I(φ²) ⊂ D(φ³) ⊂ … grows by φ³ per cycle, and each shell has one piece for every vertex, edge and face of the dual pair (12, 30, 20). The pieces are exact, at edge 1: AXE is a tetrahedron with five edges 1 and one 1/φ (two equilateral faces, two golden triangles 1, 1, 1/φ); CLEO is a triangular pyramid on an equilateral base of side 1/φ with side edges 1; FUJI is a pyramid of height 1/√3 on a flat-ended (truncated) triangle with sides 1 and 1/φ alternating and all angles 120°, with side edges 1, three equilateral and three golden faces, and a cube corner at its apex; the pentagonal pyramid has all edges 1. Every dihedral angle of the kit is, modulo 180°, an integer combination of two angles, α = arccos(√5/3) = 41.81° and δ = arctan(3 − √5) = 37.38°: the icosahedron's own is 180° − α = 138.19°, and FUJI's faces meet its base at α on the long sides and δ on the short. Because every icosahedron inside is again whole, each can be replaced by its own Lotus seed: the Chain of Karma, built and checked to 20,497 pieces. Only the icosahedron is ever subdivided: the gap pieces stay whole (they cannot be cut into the kit at one size, by the Dehn invariant) and occur at every scale φᵏ. A second exact cycle, through the icosidodecahedron, the fullerene cage and the rhombic triacontahedron, shares the dodecahedron with the Lotus seed and is described separately (Spheres of Dharma). The nesting of the dual pair at golden ratios goes back to Pacioli and Kepler and appears at every φ-power in Gray (2002); a different dodecahedral growth, with whole dodecahedra inside, is due to Al Raisi, Koca, Koca and Koc (2026). The exact shells and their endless alternation are new. Pieces and faces (edge 1). Icosahedron: 20 equilateral faces, dihedral angle 138.19° = 180° − arccos(√5/3). AXE: tetrahedron, five edges 1 and one 1/φ; 2 equilateral faces, 2 golden triangles (1, 1, 1/φ) (Mosseri–Sadoc t6 at 1/φ). CLEO: triangular pyramid, base equilateral 1/φ, side edges 1; 1 equilateral face, 3 golden triangles (Mosseri–Sadoc t4 at 1/φ). FUJI: pyramid of height 1/√3 on a flat-ended triangle (sides 1 and 1/φ alternating, angles 120°), side edges 1; 3 equilateral + 3 golden faces; apex a cube corner; faces meet the base at 41.81° (long sides) and 37.38° (short sides). Pentagonal pyramid (J2): all edges 1. J11: an icosahedron with one J2 cap removed. Every dihedral angle, modulo 180°, is a whole-number combination of α = arccos(√5/3) = 41.810° and δ = arctan(3 − √5) = 37.377°. The Lotus seed, the Chain of Karma, the pyramid tip + mirror rule and the names Lotus seed, AXE, FUJI and CLEO are DICTO's. Computation and checking were done with Claude (Anthropic) in the open-source library krp-core. Version 2 (2026-10-12): the Chain is stated as an iterated (hierarchical) dissection in which only the icosahedron is subdivided; the earlier pyramid growth rule, whose volume and Dehn identities hold for any solid, and its figure have been removed. Version 3 (2026-10-14): the paper is written in the first person throughout; no other changes. title: The Bodhi Seed: twelve rhombic triacontahedra and one more inside a triacontahedron φ² times larger, with the gap filled exactly
description: A rhombic triacontahedron RT(φ²) of edge φ² holds twelve RT(1) of edge 1, one on each five-fold axis and each pushed out until it touches the outer form, and one RT(1/φ) at its centre, without overlap. Each of the twelve touches five others face to face, in the pattern of the icosahedron's 30 edges. These are the counts and ratios of the Lotus seed (an icosahedron of edge φ² holding 12 icosahedra of edge 1 and one of edge 1/φ), and among the icosahedral solids tested on their 5-, 3- and 2-fold axes only the icosahedron and the rhombic triacontahedron close in this way. The gap, 31.8% of the volume (by volume 80 prolate and 20 oblate golden rhombohedra of edge 1, though these do not tile it), fills exactly with convex pieces in two ways, each of three types and each invariant under the full icosahedral group: kit A, 60 + 60 + 60 mirror-symmetric pieces; kit B, 60 Vajras (triangular bipyramids), 20 Crown Jewels (one in each outer three-fold corner, 14 corners) and 60 + 60 Diadems of opposite hands. Every corner is exact and every dihedral angle is a multiple of 6°. The twelve enclose exactly a rhombic hexecontahedron of edge 1 (20 prolate golden rhombohedra), so the inner pocket, the hexecontahedron minus the centre, has exactly the volume of RT(1). All pieces were checked pairwise free of overlap, with total volume exact. The layer of twelve triacontahedra around a rhombic hexecontahedron appears in S. Kabai's clusters; its closure inside RT(φ²), the centre, the exact kits and the growth as a seed were not found in the literature searched. Kit B (our names): 60 Vajra (triangular bipyramid, φ²O/6 = 0.205179), 20 Crown Jewel ((7φ − 3)O/2 = 1.957616), 60 Diadem L + 60 Diadem R (O/3 = 0.156743). Kit A : 60 Vajra, 60 B2 ((3 + 5φ)O/6 = 0.869152), 60 B3 (O/(3φ) = 0.096872). O = oblate golden rhombohedron of edge 1 (0.470228). The question, the golden-rhombohedron lead, the names and the hand-built twelve (Polyhedraverse) are DICTO's. Prior art: S. Kabai's clusters of rhombic triacontahedra around a rhombic hexecontahedron (Wolfram Demonstrations Project). Computation and checking were done with Claude (Anthropic). title: The DICTO Kepler–Poinsot–UP Cycle
description: Universal PiTet grows from the Cleo star by the tightest solid round the last, and its shells come out thin. DICTO specified a taller version ("think stellation, think Gaudí"): keep every station a true star and fill only between stars. With the icosahedron I of edge 1, the great stellated dodecahedron (spikes to 3× the face distance) has a dodecahedral hull of edge φ, the small stellated dodecahedron on that hull (spires to √5× the face distance) has an icosahedral hull of edge φ³, and the cycle repeats for ever, ×φ³ in length and ×φ⁹ in volume each turn. The spires stand φ² and φ times their face radius and the hull steps ×φ then ×φ², balancing within each turn; the stars are exactly 3× and √5× their cores in volume. Every shell is filled exactly by the Cleo star's own pattern: the spikes, inward pyramids from the hull's faces and valley tetrahedra along the core's edges. In the first shell these are DICTO's CLEO, cap and AXE. The two shells meet in golden reciprocity, PiTet's own principle of opposites: the stars' points stand φ² and φ times their face radius, and the inward pyramids of the other shell are exactly their reciprocals, 1/φ² and 1/φ. All exact in ℚ(√5). Companion to Universal PiTet (UP), DICTO DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23463305. title: Kaleidohedra by DICTO: shearable lattices, new space-fillers and the Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli (EKP) cell
description: Kaleidohedra by DICTO: working notes, verification scripts and a browser app for lattices and the polyhedra on them. This snapshot adds #21, the icosahedral octet, the MACE network and its infinite quasiperiodic version (in #20), the studies 2026-10-10-icosa-networks-2, -3, -ico-clusters and -pentagram-growth, and five short papers by DICTO (papers/: #8, #13, #14, #17, #18). #19 and #20 were first archived in v2026.10.10-icosa. All Kaleidohedra findings (DISCOVERIES.md; each checked by a script in CI; credit DICTO unless noted): DICTO skewed rhombic dodecahedron : a rhombic-dodecahedron-type space-filler whose four equal edge directions meet at 60° three times and 72° three times (60° and 72° rhombi), tiling as a sheared FCC. Not found in the literature: candidate. Equal-edge rule for sheared FCC (Kaleidohedra): the equal-edge cell of every sheared FCC lattice, by a circumcentre shift. General idea known; this form not found. Bain disphenoids become regular tetrahedra (known, Bain 1924). Bain rhombic dodecahedron : 4 squares and 8 rhombi of 60° (known). Regular-hexagon elongated dodecahedron : 4 regular hexagons, 4 squares and 4 rhombi of 60°, all edges equal, filling space by translation; Kaleidohedra's symbol. Known (the truncated octahedron with one zone removed; Grünbaum 2010, Fig. 2b); DICTO reached it independently by a new route, the Bain stretch. Exactly nine "most regular" space-fillers (Kaleidohedra two-way search): every equal-edge space-filling zonohedron whose faces are only squares, regular hexagons and 60° rhombi. DICTO skewed elongated dodecahedra (two forms), extending #1. Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli (EKP) cell , and 8b, the Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli network (below). Rhombic dodecahedron sub-family (Kaleidohedra, verified by building in Polyhedraverse): 24 sheared-FCC cells from TARGETS.md. Candidates. EKP windows : carving the six face-neighbours' stella octangulas out of the EKP cell's dodecahedron leaves exactly 12 Penrose thick rhombi (72° and 108°, edge 2/φ), one on each cube edge, each still in the dodecahedron's own face plane; 48 triangles wall the cut-away, the volume is exactly 12, and each of the six roofs keeps exactly 1/φ of itself. An aperiodic tile, at its icosahedral orientation, on a periodic cubic lattice. Not found (web-level search): candidate. Stretched dodecahedron : the dodecahedron stretched along a cube-face axis has 8 regular pentagons, 4 hexagons (108° four times, 144° twice) and 2 rectangles at any stretch, squares at a stretch of one edge; at the lattice spacing it is the hull of two face-neighbour dodecahedra. Not found (web-level search): candidate. Studies of #10 (constructions on the windows, not separate claims). 10a, the windows made convex (recorded as #12 in v2026.10.08-convex): pushing the 12 window rhombi straight out by √(7 − 4φ), keeping their size and orientation, the convex hull has 74 faces: 12 Penrose thick rhombi, 6 golden rhombi (diagonals in ratio φ) square on the cube faces, 8 equilateral triangles and 48 triangles, with only three edge lengths. The 2D and 3D aperiodic rhombi together on cubic symmetry. It unfolds into a flat net with no overlaps, so it can be built. 10b, windows and stellas in a checkerboard : the windows (even cells) and stella octangulas (odd cells) fill space exactly, each odd cube being its stella plus its six neighbours' carved roofs (each roof keeps 2/3; volumes 12 + 4 = two cubes): the stella octangula is the windows' other half. The closest prior system found (Lalvani, US 4,723,382) requires all edges on the icosahedral two-fold axes; the stella's and most wall edges are not. Star Chain Reaction (DICTO's name). Regular dodecahedra in their densest lattice packing leave one hole per cell, a Dogstar (DICTO's name; the solid itself is George W. Hart's stellation 8 of the dodecahedron, 1996, which he noted fills space alternated with regular dodecahedra). It is a partial stellation of a dodecahedron 1/φ³ the size, volume exactly φ/2 at dodecahedron edge 1. New: the EKP cell's great star is exactly the great stellated dodecahedron of that 1/φ³ core, and a whole Sunstar (a dodecahedron with the 6 Dogstars on its faces) 1/φ³ the size fits inside it with no room to grow, so dodecahedron ⊃ great star ⊃ Sunstar(1/φ³) ⊃ great star(1/φ³) ⊃ … nests forever, each step touching, ratio φ³ (the inflation factor of icosahedral quasicrystals). 12a, the Jewel chain (named the Dragon chain until 2026-10-09): each solid holds the next, every step touching. The DICTO Jewel (the windows solid, #10) holds a cube, its own core; the cube holds a stella octangula; the stella holds a Dogstar; the Dogstar holds a dodecahedron 1/φ³ the size, which holds a DICTO Jewel 1/φ³ the size, and so on: the EKP cell recurs inside its own stella. Not found in a web-level search (2026-10-08): candidate. The 13-dodecahedron cluster made solid (DICTO's cluster): a regular dodecahedron with one on each face leaves gaps of exactly two kinds, 30 wedges (two pentagons hinged at 10.3048°, volume φ³/20) and 20 needles (volume (45 − 19√5)/600); filled, it comes apart into 12 finned units and the bare centre. DICTO-Star (DICTO's own pattern, the centre of DICTO's builds by 2026-10-04): an icosidodecahedron with a regular dodecahedron on each pentagon and a tridiminished icosahedron (J63) on each triangle, 33 regular-faced pieces, every contact a whole face, every edge and corner closed, no filler, volume (195 + 89√5)/3. Not a space-filler with regular pieces (each J63 keeps an open cap). DICTO Jewel clusters (DICTO's): four DICTO Jewels in a tetrahedron (pairwise face to face, touching at one point in the middle) and six in an octahedron round a stella octangula, which fits them face for face (a solid piece); each fills space with stella octangulas, and shared they are the cells of the octet truss on the Jewels' lattice; up and down tetrahedral clusters sharing single Jewels form a Kagome (pyrochlore) network. Sunstar clusters (DICTO's): the same octet structure in the Sunstar Lattice; four dodecahedra round a cell corner, and six round an odd cell with its Dogstar inside, a solid piece (a Sunstar turned inside out); each fills space with Dogstars. The honeycomb itself is George W. Hart's (1996). #17 Kagome hulls (DICTO's): six hulls of DICTO Jewels or Sunstar dodecahedra give Kagome networks, clusters sharing single pieces corner to corner; a hull with n corners sits on a network where each cluster has n neighbours, with the icosahedral exception of #13. #18 The DICTO Hexa (DICTO's): a cube-shaped solid made of eight Hexa Jewels: DICTO Jewels set on a 2 × 2 × 2 block, passing through each other inside, so that their cube cores fill a cube of edge 4, with the 24 outer roofs on its faces (the Jewels themselves are not cubes; each holds one). With its gap, the DICTO Hexa-Key, it fills space like a checkerboard, 5 : 3. #19 The DICTO Icosa-13 (DICTO's; names by DICTO): the regular icosahedron of edge φ² (Lotus seed) is cut exactly into 12 icosahedra of edge 1, one of edge 1/φ and 100 gap pieces (60 AXE, 20 FUJI, 20 CLEO); DICTO's build from 2026-10-05 makes it from a dodecahedron + 12 gyroelongated pentagonal pyramids (J11) + 30 AXE + 20 FUJI, 63 pieces, volume (235 + 105√5)/12. UNITY, DICTO's physical 13-cell, is an icosidodecahedron + 12 J11; its 20 dimples cannot be closed by regular-faced pieces, and the convex VAJRA closes each. Also: 13 icosahedra vertex to vertex fill exactly 13/27 of their hull, and FUJI is not a union of Mosseri–Sadoc tiles at its own scale. Credited prior art: AXE and CLEO are the Mosseri–Sadoc tiles t6 and t4 scaled by 1/τ (Mosseri & Sadoc 1982); the arrangement of 12 icosahedra on a dodecahedron inside the icosahedron of edge φ² is R. W. Gray's (2002), without gap pieces. Checked in the study (not yet in CI). #20 The DICTO Stella-Corona (DICTO's; names by DICTO): an icosidodecahedron + 20 icosahedra on its triangles + 12 King of Pentacles (Tarot) on its pentagons (each a pentagonal pyramid, 10 AXE, 5 CLEO and a small pyramid, flat pentagram on top): 33 pieces like the DICTO-Star (#14), closed, every contact a whole face, volume (120 + 47√5)/3. It chains along a 3-fold axis and forms a diamond network. Closed result: there is no icosahedral Dogstar; in every lattice packing of icosahedra tested, including the densest known (Betke–Henk 0.836357), the gap is one connected labyrinth. Credited prior art: the 20-icosahedron shell is the Wolfram Demonstration "Cluster of 20 Icosahedra". title: RHOMBITURE by DICTO: an extractable golden-rhombohedron armature system for sculpture
description: RHOMBITURE (rhombus + armature) is a modular armature system for wood carving, clay modelling and mixed-media sculpture, built from the two golden rhombohedra (prolate and oblate), whose faces are all the same golden rhombus. The blocks pack into an internal core held by a temporary bond (tape, magnets or dowels) inside a permanently bonded outer crust; the artist carves or models the crust, then removes the loose core through a planned opening and reuses it. It also reports a keyed-dowel finding, checked by computation on the true 3D Penrose (Ammann–Kramer) tiling (2180 blocks, 6090 shared faces): with one marked corner per face, same-kind joins always meet marked corner to marked corner (1871/1871 prolate, 509/509 oblate), and a two-hole drilling pattern lets correct joins take dowels while a wrongly turned same-kind join takes none. First published by DICTO on 26 September 2026 in github.com/DICTOR-Master/rhombiture, disclosed openly as public prior art (no patent). The geometry and the keyed-dowel finding are verified by computation (scripts in analysis/); the physical workflow was being prototyped and not yet tested at first publication. Includes STL files and paper nets for both blocks at three golden-ratio scales. More of DICTO's geometry: https://dictospheres.com
